correctness.rationale: Construct the 15 K6 edges and 15 perfect matchings and link incidence. BFS verifies diameter 4; opposite bipartition pair distances have opposite parity for any landmark, so only 2*C(15,2)=210 same-class separation constraints matter. Independent C++ direct distance-signature exhaustive enumeration of all C(30,5)=142,506 and C(30,6)=593,775 subsets gives zero resolving five-sets and exactly 32,460 resolving six-sets. Monotonicity rules out smaller. Independent full S6 action plus incidence-checked duality generates 1,440 pairwise distinct automorphisms, while line-graph star rigidity bounds the entire group by 1,440; independent full orbit partition gives exactly 34 with sizes (180,240,360,720*18,1440*13). Independently checked full 3x3 profile: a=2 row (4230,2880,360), a=3 row (3840,7920,5760), a=4 row (4230,2880,360). Exhaustive finite reasoning applies to exactly this 30-vertex graph.
residual_risks: Numerical census specific to one fixed graph; no theorem for arbitrary generalized quadrangles.

value.rationale: The Tutte-Coxeter graph is a canonical smallest cubic girth-eight cage and distance-regular graph, and resolving sets are natural metric-identification objects. Classifying all optimal sets, their automorphism classes and bipartition statistics gives usable complete representatives and stabilizer information not mechanically implied by the known minimum size.
residual_risks: The result is an exact finite graph classification, not a new general metric-dimension bound.

final_claim: The Tutte-Coxeter 30-vertex K6 edge-vs-perfect-matching incidence graph has metric dimension 6 and exactly 32,460 metric bases; under its full automorphism group of order 1,440 those form 34 orbits (one each of sizes 180,240,360; 18 of size 720; 13 of size 1,440) and have the specified nine-coefficient bipartition/induced-edge profile.
